context: a letter from J. E. Gray, which you are answering
exchanges:
I think one can discern the “Noble Roman hand” of the great friend of John Murray, in the slashing article on the Variation of Species in the Athenæum of this date—

Thanks for the sight of Nathusius it does not come up to my expectation

I want to know why the short thin legged heavy bodied pig is called chinese or Indian as Nathusius regards it   I have not been able to discover   Buffon described a long legged bristly Pig as a Siam Pig and Schreber confuses it with the Berkshire breed & calls it S Scrofa domesticus Sinensis.—

Swinhoe thought the Chinese Pig was the tame Sus leucomystax    Natusius thinks S. leucomystax a variety of the Common Domestic Pig

If Nathusius had examined the series of skull of Wild Pig we have in the BM he would not have formed such theories   the Wild Boar of India & asiatic Island have not wider Palates than the European ones.—

But certain tame breed have an inclination to get wide palate “that is their deformity or malady”—as the Reviewer would say   I observed that in the PZS when I described Sus Pliciceps which is no doubt a Tame Pig, with the skull in many respects like Potamochœrus   Margrave says Potamochœrus was introduced from Africa to Brazil   I am assured it is not there now. Nathusius refers to it   he anticipated my observation that it is Sus Porcus of Linn S N. Ed 12 yet Du Chaillu persisted it was a new species he discovered

Ever yours sincerely | J E Gray

I sent Nathusius by the Post

Many thanks for Nathusius recd safely. When in London I will call on you & shall be much obliged if you will tell me your views on the specific differences of pigs.

I do not know who has cut me up so severely in the Ath: nor do I know whom you mean by the “great friend of John Murray.

From 2 or 3 little points I suspect the author to be your great man in the Museum—

My dear Gray | yours sincerely | Ch. Darwin
